quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended March 2026) showed a decline of sales and operating income year-on-year, mainly caused by the SPE division. But SPE order intake reached a record high level in the fourth quarter, the same situation continues in the first quarter of the new year - order levels in Q1 are probably stronger than Q4 and still increasing - and it is expected to continue into the second quarter. Advanced foundry and advanced DRAM are leading the order growth. Q4 of the prior year hit a record-high quarterly OP margin above 30% on stronger-than-expected overseas post-sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Record high SPE order intake in Q4, Q1 orders stronger than Q4; prior-year Q4 OP margin exceeded 30%

quarterly_data.signal: SPE sales are planned at JPY 260 billion in the first half and JPY 340 billion in the second half of the fiscal year. Current capacity can respond to double the second-half run rate - JPY 680 billion of annual sales - and can absorb another 10% or 20% of market growth without a new facility, covering next fiscal year. Layout and functional changes are underway at the Hikone, Kyoto and Toyama fabs; land leveling has started at the new Yasu site (between Kyoto and Hikone), with about a year until the land is flat, and a fab construction decision is needed 6-12 months ahead, with 1 to 1.5 years from decision to shipment capability. Fixed costs of JPY 32 billion this fiscal year fund growth investment under the mid-term plan (about one third is labor), with R&D, CapEx and depreciation all at record-high levels; the next mid-term plan, to be announced in spring next year, will be a harvest phase focused on improving profitability and raising ASP.
quarterly_data.figure: SPE H1 JPY 260 billion / H2 JPY 340 billion; capacity supports JPY 680 billion a year plus 10% or 20% more market growth; fixed cost JPY 32 billion; new fab 1 to 1.5 years from decision to shipment

quarterly_data.signal: Single wafer cleaning share appeared to slip in FY2025, but management said no POR was taken away - a competitor strong in BEOL cleaning recognized sales earlier (shipment basis versus SCREEN's setup basis). In FY2026 SCREEN expects market share to recover: FEOL sales (its strength) are increasing, and several customers switched a BEOL cleaning step POR from the competitor to SCREEN. The spin scrubber - a simple single wafer cleaner - is gaining share considerably, which management attributes to heavy use by the Taiwan foundry for CoWoS advanced packaging. Advanced packaging sales are expected to grow about 20% this fiscal year to over JPY 10 billion across SPE and mainly the FT segment, with many Remotia units delivered as evaluation equipment; by the year ending March 2033 advanced packaging sales are expected to reach JPY 40 billion-50 billion with much better profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced packaging sales to exceed JPY 10 billion this fiscal year (+20%), targeting JPY 40 billion-50 billion by March 2033; spin scrubber share gains on CoWoS use at the Taiwan foundry

quarterly_data.signal: China demand is stronger than at the January earnings call, though management is skeptical of competitors' forecasts of 20%-30% growth in the Chinese market; China was close to 40% of sales in the past two to three years and is expected at a little bit less than 40% this fiscal year. North America growth is driven by the Taiwanese foundry's Arizona fab and the South Korean chip manufacturer's Texas fab, with North American IDM logic investment increasing more in the second half. Pricing: annual top-management price negotiations happen between October and December; the policy is no discounting - raise ASP through better quality, functions and development capability.
quarterly_data.figure: China a little bit less than 40% of sales this fiscal year; North America lifted by the Arizona and Texas fabs
